{{Quote|There is no restraint or principle at the center of the New Order. And that is why people admire it. The Empire does all the things that people secretly believe should be done with power.|Canonhaus|<ref name="Final Order" />}}
'''Canonhaus'''<ref name="Final Order" /> was a [[human]]<ref name="Episode V" /> [[Gender|male]] who served as a [[captain]] within the [[Imperial Navy]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]] against the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. He originally served as a [[midshipman]] aboard a [[Starship|ship]] for the [[Galactic Republic]].<ref name="Episode V novel" /> During the [[Imperial Era|reign]] of the Empire, Canonhaus served as a [[lieutenant]] and participated in an [[Bombardment of Haruun Kal|insurrection on Haruun Kal]]. Later he was part of an [[Battle at Fostar Haven|attack]] on an [[Alderaanian]] refugee convoy, where he purposely filed incorrect information in his report to test whether the Empire actually cared about their problems.<ref name="Final Order" /> By [[3 ABY]],<ref name="GA" /> the [[Imperial officer]] served in [[Death Squadron]], the personal [[Fleet|armada]] of [[Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]], and was involved in the hunt for the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'' after the [[Battle of Hoth]], serving aboard the [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Ultimatum]]''.<ref name="Episode V" />

During the chase, Death [[Squadron]] was forced to move into the [[Hoth asteroid field|Hoth asteroid belt]], causing significant damage to the fleet. Eventually, Canonhaus and several other officers of the fleet reported via [[hologram]]s to [[Darth]] Vader, only to be killed during the meeting when an [[asteroid]] obliterated the [[Bridge (starship)|bridge]] of the [[Star Destroyer]] he was in.<ref name="Episode V novel" />

==Behind the scenes==
The officer debuted through hologram in the [[Star Wars saga|''Star Wars'' saga]] film [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']], albeit unidentified. In the film, the officer is portrayed by effects cameraman [[Jim Veilleux]].<ref name="Making Of TESB">''[[The Making of "The Empire Strikes Back"]]''</ref> The role was also claimed by [[Stephen Buchanan]], although Buchanan did not portray the character.<ref name="yubnub">{{WebCite|url=http://www.yubnub.de/original-trilogy/?lang=en|text=Original Trilogy Autographs|accessdate=2015-02-14|work=Yubnub.de|archivedate=20170629140005}}</ref> In the [[2020]] short-story collection ''[[From a Certain Point of View: The Empire Strikes Back]]'', the two installments "[[The Final Order]]," written by [[Seth Dickinson]],<ref name="Final Order" /> and "[[Lord Vader Will See You Now]]," written by [[John Jackson Miller]], identified the officer as Canonhaus.<ref name="Vader will see you">{{StoryCite|story=Lord Vader Will See You Now|book=From a Certain Point of View: The Empire Strikes Back}}</ref>
